title: Travel INSIDE a Black Hole
beats: Promises a trip inside a black hole, not comfortable but fun
Anything becomes a black hole if compressed enough: Everest, Earth as a peanut, you
Real black holes come from collapsed massive stars; singularity named
First question: what does it look like from outside
Sun bends starlight, funhouse-mirror galaxy ring, then simulations of lensing and Earth behind a black hole
Simple black hole with no charge or spin; you fly toward it as sky distorts; photon sphere where you could see your own head
Time warps: outside watcher sees you freeze at the horizon, redshifted; you feel nothing
Falling in: big hole is comfortable for hours; tidal difference leads to spaghettification
Unknown what happens at the singularity; maybe a wormhole
Draws two points on a sheet and folds it to show a wormhole shortcut
Dumbhole: sound version of a black hole built in labs as a testbed
Tangent: what you would see at light speed; field of view stretches
Where is the center of the universe: balloon with dots, overlay two layers at 5 percent expansion, any dot looks like the center
You are the center of the universe
Googolplex universe would contain a copy of you

metrics.misconception: partial: black holes do not suck up the galaxy behind them (2:28) and the outside view differs from your own view
metrics.examples: 5 or so (Everest, galaxy lensing, Earth orbiting, you falling, balloon); size grows from Earth to universe
metrics.ending: Detours to three loosely related ideas, ends with a teaser to Numberphile

principles.1: confirmed: starts with you, me, the camera (0:19) and Mount Everest
principles.2: partly: many terms in a row (Schwarzschild radius 0:19, photon sphere 3:22, event horizon 4:31, spaghettification 5:54) each with a one-line gloss; no formula
principles.4: confirmed: funhouse mirror for lensing (2:07), balloon for expansion (8:32); rigor step is not taken
principles.5: confirmed: 'you' fall in, and the sheet is folded by hand at 6:24
principles.7: partly: balloon overlay (9:09) lets viewer see the center appear, but he narrates the result
principles.8: contradicted: fast jumps in topic at 7:01, 7:20, 8:16, 10:02 with no slowing for novelty; the ordering is a sightseeing tour
principles.9: partly: 'you see it from outside, you see it from inside' repeated pair, and 'any dot is the center'
principles.10: partly: Everest and Earth first, stars next, whole universe last
principles.11: partly: lensing, photon sphere, horizon, tidal forces are ordered; the last third is not a dependency of the first two
principles.12: confirmed: Numberphile, acoustic black holes, wormholes, cosmological principle tie in
principles.13: partly: plain language, expert terms, but the why-this-tool is not given

new_moves.name: outside-versus-inside-view
new_moves.what: Gives each phenomenon two vantage points, observer and faller, so the learner sees the same event differently

new_moves.name: chain-of-first-questions
new_moves.what: Uses one clear question to open each segment and lets those questions hop between topics

theory: Vsauce teaches by putting you in the seat of an observer and moving that seat, which makes abstract relativity concrete without math. The weakness is that tangents pile on, so the structure is a tour, not a build.
velocity: Scene builder: render the same event from outside and from inside as paired scenes and let the tutor switch viewpoints on demand
Orchestrator: a tangent budget, since four jumps in the last four minutes lost the thread
Ghost hands: show the paper-fold wormhole as a literal gesture
quote: you really, scientifically, are the center of the universe.
